items.en: The global tyre-derived fuel (TDF) market could reach US$263.1 million by 2033, according to a Fairfield Market Research report distributed by ResearchAndMarkets. Its published summary estimates the market’s value at US$221.3 million in 2026, and forecasts compound annual growth of 2.50 per cent over the period.

In 2026, the Ballon d’Or award ceremony is heading to London for the first time. The winner of the 70th anniversary award will be announced on 26 October, and the internet is already abuzz with guesswork about who this year’s recipient will be. Something entirely free from speculation is the return of Hankook as official sponsor. The tyre maker has confirmed its sponsorship, the third consecutive year it has acted in this capacity.
Covering long-haul, regional and urban applications, the latest Kmax Gen-3 range comprises the Kmax S Gen-3 steer tyre, Kmax D Gen-3 drive tyre and Kmax T Gen-3 trailer tyre (Image: Goodyear)

Fuel efficiency and sustainability are becoming increasingly interconnected considerations for commercial vehicle fleet managers. With fleets unable to control diesel prices, Goodyear argues that reducing tyre rolling resistance offers one way to lower fuel expenditure and whole-life operating costs.

How will your next car be powered? Kwik Fit tasked market research specialist Opinium with asking UK motorists this very question, and the responses from those surveyed indicate that while combustion engines will continue to dominate in the near-term, an increasing number of motorists are considering hybrid or full electric alternatives. Kwik Fit says the findings suggest the proportion of respondents driving EVs could more than double with their next vehicle change.

National Tyre Distributors Association chief executive Ian Andrew has introduced the 12th Tyre Industry Conference at the Eastside Rooms in the heart of Birmingham, demonstrating how the association is moving forward in the second year of his leadership. The conference is themed on ‘The Tyre Professional’ this year, and Andrew’s opening remarks outlined the practical measures the association is taking to spread professionalism throughout its membership and the public acknowledgment of this professionalism in government, the media, and the broader public. This “voice of the industry” purpose is one of the two major roles Andrew identifies for the NTDA. The other, also vital in the professionalisation agenda, is as “a driver of standards.”

Joe Hinrichs has been elected chairman of the Board of Directors at The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company, effective 7 October 2026. He succeeds Laurette Koellner, who will remain a director until the company’s 2027 annual meeting, at which time she will retire in accordance with Goodyear’s Corporate Governance Guidelines. Hinrichs will also chair the board’s Governance and Executive Committees.
